questions.question: Look at the bar. It is cut into equal parts. What fraction names one part?
questions.explain: When a bar is cut into 5 equal parts, one part is 1 out of 5, so it is 1/5. The bottom number is the total parts, not just the other parts.

questions.question: A bar is cut into 3 equal parts. What fraction names one part?
questions.explain: One part out of 3 equal parts is 1 out of 3, so it is 1/3. The top number is always 1 for a unit fraction.

questions.question: Each part of this bar is one equal piece. What fraction names one piece?
questions.explain: The bar has 6 equal parts, so one piece is 1 out of 6, which is 1/6. Count all the parts for the bottom number.

questions.question: A bar is cut into 8 equal parts. What fraction names one part?
questions.explain: There are 8 equal parts, so one part is 1 out of 8, which is 1/8. A common trap is to use the 7 other parts instead of the total 8.

questions.question: Mia cut a pie into 4 equal slices. She takes one slice. What fraction of the pie is her slice?
questions.explain: The pie has 4 equal slices, so one slice is 1 out of 4, which is 1/4. The bottom number is the total slices, not the slices left over.

questions.question: Jake cuts a pizza into 6 equal slices. He eats one slice. What fraction did he eat?
questions.explain: The pizza has 6 equal slices, so one slice is 1 out of 6, which is 1/6. Count all the slices, not just the ones still on the pizza.

questions.question: A ribbon is cut into 5 equal pieces. Sam uses one piece to tie a gift. What fraction of the ribbon is one piece?
questions.explain: The ribbon has 5 equal pieces, so one piece is 1 out of 5, which is 1/5. Don't count the 4 other pieces; the bottom number is the total.

questions.question: A circle is cut into equal parts. One part is 1/5. How many equal parts make the whole?
questions.explain: If one part is 1/5, the whole is cut into 5 equal parts. A common mistake is to count the other parts (4) instead of the total (5).

questions.question: Tom says one part of a bar cut into 6 equal parts is 1/8. What did Tom get wrong?
questions.explain: The bar has 6 equal parts, so one part is 1/6. The bottom number must be 6, not 8. Tom picked the wrong total.

questions.question: A baker has 2 identical pies. She cuts each pie into 4 equal slices. What fraction of ONE pie is one slice?
questions.explain: Each pie is cut into 4 equal slices, so one slice is 1 out of 4, which is 1/4. The 2 pies is extra info; focus on just one pie.

questions.question: A bar is cut into 3 equal lengths. Each length is cut into 4 equal pieces. What fraction of the WHOLE bar is one small piece?
questions.explain: There are 3 groups of 4, so 12 small pieces make the whole bar. One piece is 1 out of 12, which is 1/12. Count every small piece for the bottom number.

questions.question: Dad cuts a long cucumber into 3 equal pieces for lunch. Leo eats one piece. What fraction of the cucumber is one piece?
questions.explain: Count all 3 equal pieces for the bottom number, so one piece is 1/3. Counting only the 2 pieces left over gives 1/2, which is wrong.

questions.question: Grandma cuts a round bannock into equal pieces for snack time. Ivy takes one piece. What fraction of the bannock is Ivy's piece?
questions.explain: Count every equal piece in the whole bannock, so one piece is 1/8. Leaving out Ivy's own piece gives 1/7, which is wrong.

questions.question: Rosa cuts her granola bar into 4 equal parts. She eats one part. What is the right way to name her part?
questions.explain: The bottom number tells how many equal parts the whole bar has, so one of 4 parts is 1/4. The 3 parts left over are not the bottom number.

questions.question: Ava's chocolate bar breaks along the lines into equal pieces. She gives one piece to her friend. What fraction of the bar is that one piece?
questions.explain: Count all the equal pieces in the whole bar, then write 1 on top for one piece: 1/6. Saying 1/2 would mean the bar has only 2 equal pieces.
